text: How is proper parthood PP(x,y) defined in classical mereology?
explanation: PP(x,y) ≡ P(x,y) ∧ x ≠ y — a part that is not the whole itself (given antisymmetry this equals P(x,y) ∧ ¬P(y,x)). Option 1 defines an improper part (part-or-equal); option 2 (P both ways) forces identity by antisymmetry; option 3 is the definition of overlap O(x,y).
